channel.title: Exploring Electronics
channel.description: Electronics from first principles — voltage, current, resistance, and circuit design explained clearly. Real components, real numbers, no prior knowledge assumed.

item.title: Package Types
item.description: Every component has a physical shape called a package. Learn the common through-hole and surface-mount families, and why this site's parts are all one kind.

item.title: Building a Threshold Ladder
item.description: Turn one sensor reading into staged, at-a-glance output. Wire three LEDs to an Arduino and light one, two, or three based on distance from baseline.

item.title: Reading an Analog Sensor
item.description: Digital pins only know HIGH and LOW. Wire an MCP9700A temperature sensor to an Arduino and use analogRead() to measure a continuous voltage instead.

item.title: Temperature Sensors
item.description: A microcontroller can only measure voltage. Learn how thermistors, analog ICs, and digital sensors each turn heat into something a circuit can read.

item.title: What Is an Arduino?
item.description: An Arduino is a tiny dedicated computer on a board. Learn what's actually on it, and how to read your first lines of Arduino code line by line.

item.title: Resistor Color Codes
item.description: A resistor has no printed numbers — just colored stripes. Learn what each band means and how to decode any resistor's value and tolerance on sight.

item.title: Blink an LED
item.description: Wire a single-LED circuit on a breadboard and flash the Blink sketch to an Arduino — your first complete loop from wiring to running code on real hardware.

item.title: Pull-up and Pull-down Resistors
item.description: An unconnected input pin floats and reads noise. How pull-up and pull-down resistors give it a steady HIGH or LOW, which to choose, and how to size one.

item.title: Digital Pins
item.description: A digital pin is either on or off — nothing in between. Learn how a microcontroller drives an LED and reads a button, and why each pin needs a resistor.

item.title: arduino-cli
item.description: Compile and upload Arduino sketches from the terminal with arduino-cli — one command, no IDE. Install it, find your board, and flash code from your own editor.

item.title: How to Read a Schematic
item.description: Learn to read electronics schematics: the standard symbols for resistors, capacitors, LEDs, and transistors, and how to trace current through any circuit.

item.title: Series and Parallel Circuits
item.description: Two wiring patterns govern every circuit ever built. Learn how series and parallel circuits work — why voltage divides in one and stays constant in the other.

item.title: Breadboards
item.description: How breadboard holes connect internally, how to use the power rails, and the wiring mistakes that kill every beginner's first circuit before it even starts.

item.title: What Is Electricity?
item.description: The label on your USB charger says 5V ⎓ 2A. Two numbers that explain how electricity works — voltage, current, resistance, and Ohm's Law explained clearly.

item.title: Home
item.description: Electronics from first principles — voltage, current, resistance, and circuit design explained clearly. Real components, real numbers, no prior knowledge assumed.
